sources_1: Jani reads coffee leaf photos. The advice is a fixed rule table. Nothing is written by a model at the moment you use it.
sources_2: Kenya has 1 extension agent for 1,380 farmers. The stated target is 1 to 600 (Ministry of Agriculture, Agriculture Extension Manual, 2025).
sources_3: Severe coffee leaf rust outbreaks in Kenya have caused yield losses above 75 percent (Gichuru and others, Agronomy, 2021).
sources_4: In Kenya, copper sprays for leaf rust start in mid-October, just before the short rains, with a second spray about three weeks later (same 2021 review).
sources_5: Rain windows for a Nyeri grid point are modelled from NASA POWER, 1991 to 2020. They are not rain-gauge readings. Treat the edges as plus or minus two weeks.
sources_6: When a trained model is added, the teaching photos are JMuBEN and JMuBEN2 from Kenya (CC BY 4.0) and BRACOL from Brazil (CC BY 4.0). This copy has no trained model yet, so there is no accuracy number.
sources_7: This tool cannot see berry disease, nutrient problems, wilt, roots, drought, or the coffee variety. It does not name a product or a dose.
sources_8: The leaf counts that count as few or many are assumptions. No Kenyan percentage threshold was found. An officer confirms them.
